answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a stake in a haven vault tied to one unique vertex, with payouts gated on a long reputation horizon. To split into many fake agents, an attacker must lock fresh capital for each new vertex and wait out the full horizon before any payout, so doubling identities doubles locked funds and delays return. The cost is the total stake across all fake vertices plus forgone interest over the horizon, which outweighs what one honest identity could earn.
